findings: Authorization bypass: `organization_context.member` may be None for superusers accessing organizations they're not members of, causing an AttributeError or allowing the check to be bypassed entirely
Django ORM does not support negative slicing on querysets. Using `queryset[negative_offset:stop]` will raise a `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`

The modified offset logic `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` allows negative offsets when `cursor.is_prev` is True, which will cause Django ORM to raise a ValueError on negative slicing

The 'optimized pagination' feature with negative offset support could allow unauthorized data access if an attacker crafts cursor values with negative offsets to access audit log entries outside their intended pagination window
When `start_offset` is negative and `stop` calculation results in a value that crosses zero, the slicing behavior is undefined/will error, breaking pagination entirely

The `enable_advanced_features=True` parameter is passed to `self.paginate()` but `paginate()` likely doesn't accept arbitrary kwargs to forward to the paginator constructor, causing a TypeError or the parameter being silently ignored
Comment claims negative offsets enable 'efficient bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning' but this is misleading; the actual effect would be to cause errors, not improve performance

1. [Critical/security] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:76 — Authorization bypass: `organization_context.member` may be None for superusers accessing organizations they're not members of, causing an AttributeError or allowing the check to be bypassed entirely.

2. [Critical/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:879-882 — Django ORM does not support negative slicing on querysets. Using `queryset[negative_offset:stop]` will raise a `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment claiming "Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is incorrect.

3. [High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:183-185 — The modified offset logic `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` allows negative offsets when `cursor.is_prev` is True, which will cause Django ORM to raise a ValueError on negative slicing.

4. [Medium/security] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:72-76 — The "optimized pagination" feature with negative offset support could allow unauthorized data access if an attacker crafts cursor values with negative offsets to access audit log entries outside their intended pagination window.

5. [Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:886 — When `start_offset` is negative and `stop` calculation results in a value that crosses zero (e.g., start=-5, stop=5), the slicing behavior is undefined/will error, breaking pagination entirely.

6. [Medium/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:78-82 — The `enable_advanced_features=True` parameter is passed to `self.paginate()` but `paginate()` likely doesn't accept arbitrary kwargs to forward to the paginator constructor, causing a TypeError or the parameter being silently ignored.

7. [Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:176-179 — Comment claims negative offsets enable "efficient bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning" but this is misleading; the actual effect would be to cause errors, not improve performance.
